value_basis: owner's manuscript (the only text with novel-sized scenes), sequential loop chaining `lc index import --next` (one call per packet plus the first `lc index packet`)
verdict: met on the owner's manuscript with the chained loop (0.108); 0.204 when every packet costs two calls (packet + import, the parallel path), just over the threshold; not met on the corpus texts, whose scenes are whole chapters (11 and 23 scenes of ~3k tokens each), so even one packet per two scenes is ~1 call per scene
detail: calls = 2 x packets (one `lc index packet` and one `lc index import` each); chained = packets + 1. Packets: entity packets of <= 6k rendered tokens (frequent names first, each naming the others' candidates) and scene packets of consecutive scenes up to 8k text tokens, never splitting a scene unless it is over 11k tokens. Gate tests: one bad quote refuses the whole answer and writes nothing; no packet of a 300k-word synthetic book exceeds 12k tokens.

synthetic-300k.note: the gate's synthetic book: corpus paragraphs repeated into chapters and scenes of 150-6000 words, one of 12000 words

owner_manuscript.note: local validation on a copy of the owner's ingested manuscript; counts only, no content
